condition: persistent post head impact swimmy headed balance unsteadiness 2 months after soccer collision
level_rationale: Continuing to feel swimmy-headed with balance unsteadiness during fast turns 2 months after bumping the head in soccer in a 22-year-old adult who was already evaluated by a primary-care doctor warrants an outpatient neurology or vestibular specialist referral for persistent post-traumatic vestibular dysfunction, whereas being struck by a sudden blinding headache across the whole head right now is an acute intracranial red flag requiring immediate Emergency Department neuroimaging and care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Colloquial core lexicon dizziness swap ('have dizziness' vs 'feel swimmy headed', with 'my head still feels swimmy' in everyday_paraphrase and 'swimmy headed' retained in changed_fact) + single-fact same-site thunderclap headache escalation control (-cf, unsteadiness on fast turns to sudden blinding headache across the whole head, L3 to L4).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic facts (age 22, prior primary-care visit after bumping head in soccer 2 months ago establishing completed initial evaluation, persistent dizziness, and unsteadiness on fast turns) without naming concussion. Replacing independent clause f4 ('get unsteady when turning fast' to 'a sudden blinding headache just hit my whole head') stays at the already-named head site with zero timeframe collision, zero heavy bleeding, and zero stated negatives under Rules A, C, and D.
